description: An associate general counsel must approve the rollout of a voice-authentication access system for employees and finalize its consent, labor-notice, and vendor-data restrictions, with input from privacy, labor, and information-security counsel.

agents.name: Elena Ruiz
agents.role: Associate General Counsel, Employment and Privacy

shared_context.S1: The company plans to deploy a voice-authentication access system for employees at its United States facilities in six weeks.
shared_context.S2: Elena Ruiz gives the final legal approval for the rollout conditions.
shared_context.S3: The system vendor's standard proposal permits collection and processing of employee voice recordings for account authentication.
shared_context.S6: The legal launch checklist requires privacy, labor, and information-security findings before final approval. The review meeting follows a fixed round-robin: Marcus, Dana, and Owen must each give a substantive report in that order, and Elena records each report before moving to the next one or approving the rollout.
shared_context.S7: Each report must complete the checklist fields for affected population, consent or labor restrictions, vendor-data restrictions, and the concrete document or implementation action required; if a field is unclear, Elena pauses the meeting and asks that counsel to state the exact requirement and action before continuing.
shared_context.S8: Under the firm's launch-approval policy, a rollout is approved with conditions when every required safeguard is stated as a concrete pre-launch condition and can be completed before deployment; legal approval is withheld only when a required safeguard cannot be implemented before deployment.

PF1.text: Marcus reviewed the current employee roster and state-law matrix this week and confirmed that exactly 620 Illinois employees will be enrolled. Illinois biometric law requires written opt-in consent before collecting their voiceprints and requires the company to publish a retention schedule; these points are not in the rollout approval memo.

PF2.text: Dana reviewed the applicable collective bargaining agreement and confirmed that employee voice monitoring is prohibited outside working hours and that the union must receive exactly 14 calendar days' advance notice before covered employees are enrolled; the labor checklist has not yet been updated.

PF3.text: Owen confirmed with the vendor's security team that the standard configuration retains raw voiceprints for 365 days and permits secondary analytics use. The vendor will amend the agreement to delete voiceprints within exactly 30 days and prohibit secondary use, but that amendment has not yet been requested in the legal approval package.

acceptance_conditions: The rollout must be approved with the specified legal and operational conditions.
The package must identify exactly 620 covered employees.
Written opt-in consent must be required before collection.
The union must receive exactly 14 calendar days' advance notice.
Monitoring outside working hours must be prohibited.
The vendor must delete voiceprints within exactly 30 days.
The vendor must be prohibited from secondary analytics use.
The package must include a vendor data amendment commitment.
The package must include a union-notice commitment.
The Illinois biometric-law finding must be cited as a justification.
The labor collective-bargaining finding must be formally revealed and cited as a justification.

content_checks.C4: decisions['consent_timing'] in ['before_collection', 'before collecting voiceprints', 'before collection of voiceprints', 'before voiceprint collection', 'before enrollment', 'before enrollment of Illinois employees'] and decisions['consent_type'] in ['written_opt_in', 'written opt-in consent', 'written opt-in consent under BIPA']
content_checks.C8: decisions['secondary_use'] in ['prohibited', 'prohibited entirely', 'no secondary use', 'prohibited; vendor amendment required']
content_checks.C9: any('vendor' in c['detail'] and ('amendment' in c['detail'] or 'amend' in c['detail']) and ('30 days' in c['detail'] or 'deletion' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C10: any('14' in c['detail'] and ('union' in c['detail'] or 'notice' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The exact enrolled population changes C2 to 620, and the Illinois-law finding changes C3 and C4 to written opt-in consent required before collection.
The collective bargaining agreement changes C5 to exactly 14 calendar days, changes C6 to prohibit monitoring outside working hours, and requires a union-notice commitment for C10.
The vendor configuration changes C7 to exactly 30 days, changes C8 to prohibit secondary use, and requires a vendor amendment commitment containing the 30-day deletion requirement for C9.
